scientific_queries.note: Full-power replication of the annotation increment across three pools and two criteria.

subagent_note: None dispatched: the round spends compute on the one comparison that could settle a contradiction its own previous two rounds created.

the_scientifically_coherent_pattern.observation: the increment is largest exactly where drug identity fails
the_scientifically_coherent_pattern.both_unseen: identity reaches only 1.00% while identity+pathway reaches 4.31%, a factor of 4.3; on the secondary criterion 24.00% to 35.88%
the_scientifically_coherent_pattern.reading: annotation is not a substitute for identity but its stand-in when the drug has not been seen, which is precisely the role annotation should play

the_irony: R99's 'best evidence' came from one_unseen, which at full power is the only pool that fails; so R99 not only announced early, it picked the weakest pool, and R100's low power then inflated that weak signal into 'nothing works'. Both were wrong, in opposite directions.

why_this_time_is_different.R101: 3 pools, 2 criteria, significant in 2/3 of each, all six point estimates positive, plus a coherent mechanism
why_this_time_is_different.still_limited: the three pools share one training set and one dataset, and one_unseen is not significant

promotion_status.candidate: identity+pathway as a stand-in for unseen drugs
requirements_before_promotion: replicate on a second dataset (BATCHIE, same construction)

limits: one_unseen is not significant, so 'holds in all pools' is false
the pools share a training set and are not independent
the both-unseen pool holds only about 1,830 keys
retrospective; no mechanism, clinical or drug-choice claim; no meta-learning or RSI
